page: Microsoft Azure D4plds_v7 is an ARM64 virtual machine within the Dpldsv7 series, provisioned through Microsoft Hyper-V. The platform features 4 dedicated 64-bit ARM vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The configuration includes 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside support for Azure Premium Storage remote volumes. The instance includes no discrete graphics processing units.

Hardware resource distribution prioritizes processor density over broad memory allocation. The 1:2 core-to-RAM ratio minimizes unused memory footprint for execution threads, yielding efficient utilization for scale-out applications. The bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD serves as high-speed scratch space for temporary data, logs, and build artifacts, removing IOPS strain from remote block storage volumes.

Operational tradeoffs include the requirement for arm64 binary compatibility, which demands native operating systems, runtimes, and application packages. With total RAM limited to 8.0 GB, memory-bound workloads and large in-memory caching systems are constrained. In addition, the configuration provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring virtual network routing or separate IP allocation for external communication.

The D4plds_v7 instance delivers cost efficiency for compute-dense architectures with low per-thread memory requirements. Primary workload fits include CI/CD build agents, containerized microservices, application worker nodes, lightweight batch processing routines, and distributed web serving tiers built for 64-bit ARM environments.
description: Microsoft Azure D4plds_v7 is an ARM64 virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory at a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes equipped with 236 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage attachments, with no GPU hardware present. By pairing dedicated 64-bit ARM compute with a lean memory footprint, the server delivers high compute density for scale-out architectures without incurring excessive memory overhead. Tradeoffs include application dependencies on the arm64 instruction set, memory ceilings for caching workloads, and the absence of bundled public IPv4 addresses. The high-speed local NVMe storage provides rapid scratch and swap space for disk-intensive operations. D4plds_v7 is best fitted for microservices, continuous integration runners, web frontends, and distributed worker pipelines.
